5. The case of the defendant Nos.1 to 6, in short, is that the suit land belonged to the khas possession of then Zaminder Babu Khamata Kinkar Roy of Showapur, PS Dhamria whose interest was that of a tenure holder in respect of the suit property and his name was recorded as such in the CS khatian and in the relevant registers and that while having such tenure interest, the said Zaminder by an unregistered amalnama dated 15th Poush 1344 BS settled the suit land to Md Abdul Gafur, who took physical possession of the said land after obtaining such allotment and since then they have been possessing the land by annually selling the jungles to the buyers who took the same for cutting and taking away the shrubs and trees for use as fuel. It is further contended that Abdul Gafur died leaving 6 sons namely, Serajul Islam, Furat Ali, Abdul Balek, Noya Miah, Chanda Lai and Elihi Box; that the heirs of Abdul Gafur were also in possession of suit land; that Serajul Islam and the other heirs of Serajul Islam filed Title Suit No. 329 of 1974 against the Department of Forest for permanent injunction restraining them from disturbing their peaceful possession; that summons of that suit was properly served; that the learned Government pleader appeared and filed written statement but lastly, he did not turn up and ultimately the suit was decreed ex parte on 4-12-1975. 

 36. Moreover, the law relating to the retention of khas land in the possession of tenant is envisaged in the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1951. 

 37. Section 43 of the Act provides for publishing a notification declaring that compensation assessment roll in respect of any village or group of villages or local area has been finally published. Sub-section (3) of section 44 of the Act provides that all interests of raiyats etc. in non-retainable khas land other than the interest which has already been acquired under any other provision of the Act i.e. section 3 under Chapter II or sub-section 3 of section 46E shall be deemed to have been acquired by the government and vest absolutely in the government free from all encumbrances from the first day of the agricultural year next following the date of publication in the official Gazette. On the other hand, sub-section 1 of the said section 44 provides that all interest of rent receivers in the estates, tenures and all other rent receiving interests in any holding or tenancy or in the non-retainable khas land other than the interest already acquired under Chapter-II or sub-section 3 of section 46E shall be deemed to have been acquired by the government and vest absolutely in the government from the first day of the agricultural year next following the date of publication of such notification in the official gazette. Thus, reading of section 20, 43, and 44 of the Act together, we have no option but to hold that non-retainable khas land belonging either to the rent receiver or to the tenant shall be deemed to have been acquired by the Government and vested in the government with the publication of a notification about final publication of the compensation assessment roll in the official gazette from the first day of the agricultural year next following the date of publication of such notification. 

 38. Sub-section (1) of section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act provides that "on the acquisition of interest of rent receivers in any area under Chapter V, no rent receiver, cultivating raiyat, cultivating under-raiyat of non-agricultural tenant shall be entitled to retain possession of any of his khas lands in such area except as provided in sub-section,(2)." 

 39. Under sub-section (2) of section 20 of the said Act, persons mentioned in sub-section (1) above are entitled to retain possession of one hundred (now sixty) standard bighas of land as tenant under the government. Now there is no scope for retaining possession of non-retainable Khas land by any tenant in Bangladesh on any ground whatsoever. 

 40. In the facts and circumstance of the case and evidence on record, we are inclined to hold that the defendants-respondents obtained the ex parte decree in Title Suit No. 329 of 1974 suppressing summons collusively and practising fraud upon the Court. Again, the defendants-respondents manufacturing some false and concocted amalnama dhakhilas and khatians tried to validate the evil design of grabbing huge quantum of the forest khas land practising fraud upon the Court and their evil design has been revealed in the appeal. The essence of law being to advance the cause of justice and not to frustrate it. If fraud is allowed to be perpetratect and perpetuated the sanctity attached to law will wither away with disastrous consequences to the society. The case of the defendants-respondents is the glaring example of committing fraud upon the Court which cannot be encouraged.
